issues.title: README.md's Usage Example does not compile (nonexistent Graphics/GraphicsDeviceManager.hpp include, unqualified CornflowerBlue) and presents every frame twice
issues.summary: The README's game skeleton includes a nonexistent header path, writes CornflowerBlue without Color::, and calls device.Present() in Draw although EndDraw() already presents, so the copied program fails to compile and, once repaired, presents twice per frame.
issues.public_contract: README.md section 10 (Usage Example): the minimal Game skeleton; Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GraphicsDeviceManager.hpp, Color::CornflowerBlue and the Game::Draw / EndDraw presentation contract
issues.expected: The README's “Minimal XNA-style game skeleton” is the first program most users copy. It should compile against the public headers and follow the frame contract CNA shares with XNA: Game::Tick calls BeginDraw(), Draw() and EndDraw(), and {{src:modules/runtime/src/GraphicsDeviceManager.cpp|GraphicsDeviceManager::EndDraw}} presents, so a Draw override never calls Present() itself. CNA's own {{src:modules/renderers/stub/examples/stub_smoke_test.cpp|stub_smoke_test.cpp}} states exactly that rule (“No explicit Present() here”).
issues.actual:
At 009d40f5 the example in {{src:README.md|README.md}}:

  • includes Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/GraphicsDeviceManager.hpp; the only such header is {{src:modules/runtime/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GraphicsDeviceManager.hpp|Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GraphicsDeviceManager.hpp}} and no forwarding header exists anywhere in the tree;
  • calls device.Clear(CornflowerBlue) with only using namespace Microsoft::Xna::Framework and Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics in effect, but CornflowerBlue is the static member Color::CornflowerBlue ({{src:modules/math/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Color.hpp|Color.hpp}}) and no namespace-scope name exists;
  • ends Draw with device.Present(). {{src:modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp|Game::Tick}} then calls EndDraw(), GraphicsDeviceManager::EndDraw calls GraphicsDevice::Present() again, and {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice::Present}} has no once-per-frame guard, so the renderer's Present() runs twice every frame.

The overrides also skip Game::Update and Game::Draw, which update and draw registered components and call FrameworkDispatcher::Update(); harmless in this component-free skeleton, but it drops the base-call pattern of the XNA template. The rest of the example (GraphicsDeviceManager(Game*), the CNAEXT Texture2D(path, device) constructor and SpriteBatch::Draw(texture, x, y)) matches the headers.

issues.title: misc/cnj.md and xnb.md say the content manifest services ResolveAssetPath's existence checks; ContentManager still probes the live filesystem on every Load
issues.summary: CNA's CNJ and XNB design notes describe the startup content-manifest scan as the cache that replaces ResolveAssetPath's std::filesystem::exists calls, but at TARGET the manifest is an introspection snapshot that Load<T> never consults.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::Load<T> / ResolveAssetPath resolution and ContentManager::GetContentManifest / RefreshContentManifest, as described by misc/cnj.md and xnb.md
issues.expected: CNA's design notes describe the resolution path as implemented. {{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManager.hpp|ContentManager.hpp}} itself records the current contract at contentManifest_: the manifest is “NOT yet consulted by ResolveAssetPath()/Load<T>()'s own exists()-based resolution”, and wiring it in is “deliberately deferred” so that ContentManager keeps noticing a file the instant it is written.
issues.actual: {{src:misc/cnj.md|misc/cnj.md}} (the resolution-order rationale) says the extra failed .cnj existence check is “negligible, and now serviced by the content-manifest cache (see xnb.md's ‘Content manifest’ section) rather than a raw stat call”, and a later bullet calls the scan “an internal performance cache”. {{src:xnb.md|xnb.md}} (“Content manifest: startup Content-root scan”) says the manifest “replaces” ResolveAssetPath's per-candidate std::filesystem::exists() calls with one upfront walk, and that a file added after the scan is not found until RefreshContentManifest(). At TARGET, ResolveAssetPath (inline in ContentManager.hpp) calls std::filesystem::exists for the literal path, for the .cnj candidate and for each extension candidate, each after ResolveExistingAssetPath's live case-insensitive directory walk ({{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp|ContentManager.cpp}}); the .xnb/.cnb probes before it use the same walk. The manifest is built only by GetContentManifest()/RefreshContentManifest(). Read together, the notes imply that Load<T> would miss a file added after the scan; in fact Load<T> finds it immediately, and only GetContentManifest() is a snapshot.

sources.note: resolution-order rationale paragraph and the content-manifest scan bullet

manifest tests; none ties Load to the manifest

The header comment and the code agree with each other and contradict both notes. The companion claim of a global cnjVersion ceiling of 1 is no longer made: misc/cnj.md documents per-type ceilings. None of these files changed between the manuscript's pin and TARGET.

Nothing checks the design notes, and no test relates Load<T> to the manifest, which is correct for the current contract.

issues.workaround: Trust the contentManifest_ comment in ContentManager.hpp and the site's {{page:deep-dives/content/contentmanager-resolution-rules.html#manifest|resolution rules}}: Load<T> never consults the manifest.

issues.title: docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md says XNA resources own a unique_ptr renderer (naming a non-existent ITexture2DRenderer) and that sharing never reaches the public API; Texture2D copies share a shared_ptr renderer
issues.summary: The document's Ownership Model describes unique_ptr renderer ownership, but Texture2D, Texture3D and TextureCube hold shared_ptr renderers and Texture2D's public defaulted copies share the renderer and CPU shadow.
issues.public_contract: docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md section 1 (Ownership Model) against Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::Texture2D (copy constructor, copy assignment, GetRendererWeak, GetCpuPixelsWeak), Texture3D and TextureCube
issues.expected: The lifetime document describes the ownership that the resource classes implement, so that a maintainer reasoning about disposal, copies and native-handle retention starts from the right model.
issues.actual: {{src:docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md|graphics-resource-lifetime.md}} section 1 says existing XNA resources hold a std::unique_ptr<IXxxRenderer>, gives ITexture2DRenderer as an example, and says any sharing (as in Texture2DArray) “never reaches the public API”. At TARGET no type named ITexture2DRenderer exists under modules/. {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Texture2D.hpp|Texture2D.hpp}} holds std::shared_ptr<ITextureRenderer> renderer_, a shared cpuPixels_ vector and shared extraMipLevels_; its public CNAEXT copy constructor and copy assignment are defaulted and documented as sharing “the underlying texture resource”, and GetRendererWeak()/GetCpuPixelsWeak() hand out weak references. {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Texture3D.hpp|Texture3D.hpp}} and {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/TextureCube.hpp|TextureCube.hpp}} hold std::shared_ptr renderers too. The unique-ownership rule holds for {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/VertexBuffer.hpp|VertexBuffer}} and {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/IndexBuffer.hpp|IndexBuffer}}, which is the shape the document's section 5 move example uses.

issues.title: PacketReader::ReadColor and PacketWriter::Write(Color) doc comments still say ReadColor reads four floats and is not the inverse of Write(Color)
issues.summary: Since c4561fd2b ReadColor reads the four bytes Write(Color) writes and a test asserts the round trip, but both public header comments and a test-file comment still describe a four-float asymmetry preserved from 'upstream', which XNA 4.0 itself does not have.
issues.expected: The public header documentation describes the implemented wire format: Write(Color) writes R, G, B, A as four bytes and ReadColor() reads them back, so the two are inverses. XNA 4.0 agrees: its PacketWriter.Write(Color) writes Color.PackedValue as a uint and PacketReader.ReadColor() reads a uint into PackedValue (IL of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net).
issues.actual: {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/PacketReader.cpp|PacketReader::ReadColor}} reads four bytes, with a comment explaining the 2026-09-04 correction (c4561fd2b), and PacketReaderTest.ReadColorReadsFourBytesAndInvertsWriteColor asserts the round trip. Yet {{src:modules/net/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Net/PacketReader.hpp|PacketReader.hpp}} still documents ReadColor as “Reads a Color value as four 32-bit floats” and “Not the inverse of PacketWriter::Write(Color) … Preserved as-is for behavioral fidelity”, {{src:modules/net/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Net/PacketWriter.hpp|PacketWriter.hpp}} says Write(Color) is “Not the inverse of PacketReader::ReadColor(), which reads four floats”, and the block comment above WriteColorWritesFourBytes in {{src:modules/net/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Net/PacketReaderWriterTests.cpp|PacketReaderWriterTests.cpp}} says ReadColor reads 4 floats and Color is not round-trippable, directly above the test that proves the opposite.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. The XNA 4.0 contract was checked in the IL disassembly of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net (PacketReader::ReadColor calls BinaryReader::ReadUInt32 and Color::set_PackedValue; PacketWriter::Write(Color) writes get_PackedValue through BinaryWriter::Write(uint32)), so the headers' “upstream” asymmetry is not XNA's behaviour either. Header and test-comment drift, not a behaviour defect.
issues.tests_current: PacketWriterTest.WriteColorWritesFourBytes and PacketReaderTest.ReadColorReadsFourBytesAndInvertsWriteColor pin the corrected behaviour; nothing checks the comments.
issues.regression_test: Documentation fix: both Doxygen blocks should say four bytes, R, G, B, A, inverse of each other, matching XNA's packed value; delete the stale block comment in the test file.
issues.blast_radius: Users of the networking API reading the public headers, who would expect ReadColor to consume sixteen bytes and might write four floats to feed it, which now misreads the packet. No runtime behaviour is affected.
issues.workaround: Treat Write(Color)/ReadColor() as a four-byte round trip, as the implementation and {{page:deep-dives/services/network-sessions.html#packets|the packet notes}} describe.

issues.title: misc/CNAEXT.md's 'Renderer shader coverage for PBR' table omits OPENGL4 and METAL and still says WebGPU has no SkinnedPbrEffect path
issues.summary: The table lists seven renderer rows and a fallback row, but OPENGL4 and METAL implement both PBR effects, WebGPU implements skinned PBR, and FNA3D and PORTABLEGL refuse PBR draws by name, none of which it shows.
issues.public_contract: misc/CNAEXT.md section 3.1, 'Renderer shader coverage for PBR' (PbrEffect / SkinnedPbrEffect per renderer)
issues.expected: The table states, for the current renderer set, which renderers draw PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect, which fall back and which refuse.
issues.actual:
{{src:misc/CNAEXT.md|misc/CNAEXT.md}} lists EasyGL, Vulkan, SdlGpu, WebGPU (“unskinned”, “no skinning path yet”), D3D11, D3D9/D3D12 and a fallback row. At TARGET:

  • OPENGL4 builds StockProgramShape::Pbr and StockProgramShape::PbrSkinned stock programs ({{src:modules/renderers/opengl4/src/OpenGL4StockDraw.cpp|OpenGL4StockDraw.cpp}});
  • METAL carries PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect shader paths (METAL-81, METAL-82 in {{src:modules/renderers/metal/src/MetalRenderer.mm|MetalRenderer.mm}});
  • WebGPU creates and draws skinned PBR (CreateSkinnedPbrResources, DrawFamily::SkinnedPbr, IssueSkinnedPbrDraw in {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp|WebGPURenderer.cpp}}), so the “no skinning path yet” cell is stale;
  • FNA3D refuses a PBR draw through RequirePbrShadingSupportEXT ({{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dDraw.cpp|Fna3dDraw.cpp}}) and PORTABLEGL refuses PbrEffect by name ({{src:modules/renderers/portablegl/src/PortableGLRenderer.cpp|PortableGLRenderer.cpp}}); neither appears in the table, whose last row suggests every unlisted renderer silently falls back.

CNA's own {{src:misc/FUTURE.md|misc/FUTURE.md}} counts 17 PBR renderers (15 apply COLOR_0, 2 refuse), far more than the table shows.
